summary: Critical CPU and memory spike correlated with traffic surge on web-01 in us-east-1. CPU peaked at 95.1% and memory grew by 62% over 50 minutes, coinciding with a 4x increase in HTTP request volume starting at 14:15 UTC.
root_cause: Traffic surge caused resource exhaustion on web-01. HTTP requests increased from 1200/5min to 5100/5min (4.25x), overwhelming the single instance's capacity. Memory growth pattern suggests potential memory leak under high load conditions.
evidence: CPU usage spiked from 45.2% to 95.1% between 14:00 and 14:40 UTC
Memory increased from 2.0GB to 3.5GB (62% growth) in the same period
HTTP requests surged from 1200 to 5100 per 5-min interval (4.25x increase)
CPU and traffic spikes are temporally correlated (traffic spike preceded CPU spike by ~5 min)
Memory did not decrease proportionally when traffic subsided, suggesting a potential leak
recommendations: Immediately: Scale horizontally by adding instances behind the load balancer
Set up CPU-based auto-scaling with threshold at 75% to prevent future saturation
Investigate potential memory leak — memory grew 62% but didn't recover with reduced traffic
Add circuit breaker pattern for upstream services to prevent cascade failures
Configure alerting for CPU > 80% and memory growth > 50% in 30 minutes
anomalies_detected: CPU reached 95.1% at 14:40 UTC — significantly above normal baseline of ~50%
Memory grew monotonically from 2.0GB to 3.5GB without recovery, suggesting a leak
Traffic spike to 5100 req/5min at 14:30 — 4.25x the baseline of 1200 req/5min
